bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the PMC article header
bibliography.note: Sand-Jensen, K., Pedersen, O., Binzer, T. & Borum, J. 2005. Contrasting oxygen dynamics in the freshwater isoetid Lobelia dortmanna and the marine seagrass Zostera marina. Annals of Botany 96(4): 613-623 (published online 18 July 2005).

claims.claim: In a water lobelia lawn in a Swedish sandy lake, more than 97 % of photosynthetic O₂ left through the roots, and root respiration used only about a fourteenth of it
claims.source_value: Both figures are from earlier laboratory split-chamber experiments that the authors summarise in their Discussion (roots in O₂-depleted water, in the light), not from the Swedish lawn: root release was 'over 97 % of the total release' by photosynthesis in L. dortmanna (1 % in Zostera), and root respiration consumed '14 times less than root release'.
claims.location: web page (PMC), Discussion, paragraph beginning 'Previous experiments in split-chambers'
claims.quote: over 97 % of the total release in L. dortmanna
claims.conditions: split-chamber laboratory experiments ('Previous experiments in split-chambers have revealed…'; the paragraph cites Sand-Jensen & Prahl 1982 for root O₂ permeability); the 1/14 is root respiration relative to root release
claims.note: The ratio is right ('14 times less than root release'), but both numbers are laboratory results, not measurements in the lawn. Rewrite: 'In split-chamber experiments, more than 97 % of the O₂ water lobelia released in the light left through its roots, and root respiration used about a fourteenth of that; in a Swedish lawn, porewater at 4 cm stayed oxic day and night.'

claims.claim: porewater at 4 cm stayed oxic day and night (water lobelia lawn, Swedish sandy lake)
claims.location: web page (PMC), Results/Discussion on field O₂ dynamics; Fig. 2 caption
claims.quote: Oxygen was present throughout the day and night at 40 mm depth
claims.conditions: oligotrophic Lake Skånes Värsjö, Sweden; L. dortmanna on sandy sediment at 50 cm water depth; two microelectrodes at 40 mm in the sediment, recorded from afternoon through the night to late morning (one diel cycle); O₂ ranged 21-3 kPa (≈100-10 % of air saturation) near a root and 10-3 kPa (≈50-10 %) farther away
claims.note: Oxic, but falling to about 10 % of air saturation by late night.

claims.paper: §3.4.2, Table 3.4-1 (isoetid rosette row) and its sources line
claims.claim: water lobelia lawn ~90 g DW m⁻² and ~28,000 roots m⁻² (Sweden)
claims.source_value: 90 g DW m⁻² is the maximum summer biomass the authors assume for a dense L. dortmanna population ('Maximum biomass during summer can reach about 90 g'; no site given; also the basis of Table 1), and ~28,000 roots m⁻² is their calculation for such a population from the weight and root number of the plants studied (Lake Skånes Värsjö, Sweden), not a count
claims.quote: the dense L. dortmanna populations will contain about 28 000 roots per m
claims.conditions: calculated values for a dense population of 90 g DW m⁻² (mean root spacing ≈ 5 mm; root surface 3.6 m² and leaf surface 2.2 m² per m² of sediment, Table 1)
claims.note: Write 'up to ~90 g DW m⁻² in dense summer populations, ≈ 28,000 roots m⁻² (calculated)'.

tried.note: refused to the script; the PMC HTML was used instead

notes: Other values: L. dortmanna reaches about one-third of the Secchi depth, at ~40 % of surface irradiance; photosynthesis at saturating light 1-2 mg O₂ g⁻¹ DW h⁻¹; lacunal gas 10.5 cm³ g⁻¹ DW, holding ~3.0 mg O₂ g⁻¹ DW at air saturation (5-10 h of respiration); a 90 g m⁻² population holds ~945 cm³ gas and 265 mg O₂ per m² (Table 1); porosity of lobelia sands 40-45 %; enrichment with degradable organic matter lowers sediment O₂ and plant growth (Christensen & Sand-Jensen 1998, cited).
